articleTitle: Brief review on journey of secured hash algorithms
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: A detailed review of a brief history, applications and contributions of the hash functions in today's cryptology are articulated here. The secured hash functions are applied in various fields to provide a secure data transfer and authentication of messages and other user linked information through a series of algorithms. From the establishment of the first hash function MD5, followed by SHA 1, this data encryption system has undergone several upgradations and advanced to SHA 2 and SHA 3, the details of which are discussed in this paper. The importance of the secure hash algorithm in network security and also the necessity to upgrade from SHA1 and SHA2 to the modern standards of SHA3 is also highlighted here.

articleTitle: Dermatological effect of UV rays owing to ozone layer depletion
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In recent years, one of the major threat for the earth is the depletion of ozone layer that accelerates the incoming amount of various solar rays including the UV rays. It has an drastic effect on the health of different living organisms most prominently on the skin. There are several reasons for which ozone hole is being created and increased continuously. In recent days, an increasing awareness can be noticed and different countries are showing their concern on this issue. It is also one of the reasons for global warming and different climate changes that can indirectly. Besides various effects, one of the major threats caused by solar radiation is the skin cancers. In United Kingdom, higher temperature can be observed during the summer period along with some temperature events. This can cause serious issues that can be harmful for the total population. An ozone hole can be observed at the Antarctic region. A notable increase in UV-B has been reported in Punta Arenas, Chile which also known as the south most city. So, the rate of depletion of the ozone layer must be reduced. Moreover, skin related diseases should be detected early so that proper treatment can be given. In this work, effects of ozone hole are being studied on the skin.

articleTitle: A fuzzy AHP-based relay node selection protocol for Wireless Body Area Networks (WBAN)
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Wireless Body Area Networks are highly localized wireless networks which include sensors that may be placed in the human body or surface mounted on the body in particular places. This type of network can potentially support a variety of medical applications from tracking vital signs to monitoring the functioning of implants as well as providing electronic services. It faces numerous challenges like of frequent link loss due to postural body movement, size and complexity of the sensors, channel condition and power consumption. In this paper we deal with such type of two-hop star topology extension of IEEE 802.15.6 (WBAN) which supports multiple relays where relay node selection becomes an interesting area of concern. Many existing research works emphasized the problem but none of them considered the fuzziness of the decision makers. This paper provides a Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process (FAHP) based relay node selection scheme that prioritizes the vagueness of the decision makers during the relay node selection procedure. The proposed scheme can intensively meet both of the requirements of WBAN i.e. enhanced reliability of the communication systems and optimum consumption of power.

articleTitle: An integrated method for automated biomedical image segmentation
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Automated biomedical image segmentation is one of the major research area. In this work an integrated approach has been developed for automated biomedical image segmentation. Level set image segmentation method has been employed for automated biomedical image segmentation. Level set algorithm needs to be configured appropriately i.e. its parameters should be properly adjusted. Manual participation sometimes required for proper adjustment of these values. To overcome this issue, a fuzzy clustering has been employed to for initial segmentation. The controlling parameters of level set method can be computed using the fuzzy clustering method. This method enhances efficiency of the level set method.

articleTitle: Optimal usage of pessimistic association rules in cost effective decision making
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Strength of an association rule is expressed in terms of interest between antecedent and consequent which is measured by using objective interestingness measures. The rules that contain at least user defined minimum interestingness are treated as Strong Association Rules (SAR). All of the SARs, extracted from the same database have no equal importance in knowledge discovery. As the user has limited resource to fix up the minimum interestingness, so there is a chance of generation of some SARs with high dissociation. Conceptually dissociation is opposite of association. As a matter of fact this type of SARs has pessimistic significance in knowledge discovery. It seems that some of the SARs are not really strong rules. This paper tries to find out such type of pseudo SARs termed as Pessimistic Association Rules (PAR). Dealing with PARs may not satisfy the user's expectation in decision making. Thus rejection of PARs may lead to a cost effective way to get a concrete decision. Experimental analysis proves the effectiveness of the proposed concept.

articleTitle: A decision framework of IT-based stream selection using Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) for admission in technical institutions
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: We face varieties of problems and multitude of decisions every day. As a result decision making has become very tough, so that all the requirements can be met in an efficient way. Some of these decisions are relatively small, take a split-second and others are big, take a long time and can have a major influence in the course of our life. So we need a proper decision making way or strategy to stop us becoming prey to a number of common fallacies, biases, and other decision-making errors. Selection of stream or trade or discipline in engineering college is one of such important decisions for a student that claim to be very proper. Hence, in this paper we have proposed a new application of Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) based decision making method invented by T Saaty, for Information Technology (IT)-based stream selection during admission in engineering or technical colleges where rank, class XII or equivalent exam marks, science related projects, and coding proficiency are considered as the selection parameters. In this paper we have restricted ourselves in stream selection only. The selection of colleges can be done by using same approach.

articleTitle: Bag-of-features based classification of dermoscopic images
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Dermoscopy image analysis is one of the open challenge and important issue related to biomedical image analysis. Determination of different diseases of skin is necessary in medical practices. Automated techniques are proved to be useful in detection and classification process of different skin diseases. There are several automated computer guided tools and frameworks have been proposed for early detection and analysis of skin diseases. In this work a comprehensive study on dermoscopic image analysis using bag-of-features has been presented. Bag-of-features is one of the well-known classification method. It uses local description of images. In case of dermoscopy image analysis, color and texture plays a vital role. Color and texture descriptors have been also discussed. Future directions in dermoscopy image analysis based on bag-of-features model are also presented.

articleTitle: Internet of Things and cognitive radio — Issues and challenges
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a promising subject of technical, social, and economic implication. The primary aspect of IoT is different objects are being combined with internet connectivity with powerful data analytic capabilities. The concept IoT is all about connecting various devices and sensors to the internet i.e. IoT is a world wide network of interconnected objects, but it is not always palpable how to provide the inter connectivity. On the basis of some studies, it is seen that the impact of IoT on the internet and economy are very inspiring which includes great global economic impact by next few years. IoT is capable to establish interconnectivity of objects through mainly, wireless communication technologies as cost-effectiveness issues and accessibility to remote users make wireless communication as a feasible solution but IoT paradigm pretenses new challenges to the communication technology as several objects of heterogeneous in nature will need to be connected and one of the major challenge is the scarcity of available spectrum to establish the connectivity. To address these issues new radio technologies and network architectures need to be thought of to accommodate several future devices having connectivity demands and consequently trends are shifting to the network which is intelligent enough to adapt with the ambience i.e. Cognitive Radio(CR) Networks and introduction of CR into IoT can improve the efficiency of the spectrum. This paper explores the possibility to put forward the application prospect of the cognitive radio-based platform into IoT.

articleTitle: ECG beat quality assessment using Self Organizing Map
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Electrocardiograms (ECG) are cardiac signals formed by the cyclical electrical activity of the heart muscles. The signal is very important for cardiovascular disease assessment. However, in ambulatory monitoring, artifacts are generated quite often which corrupts the ECG beats. This makes the efficient analysis of the biomedical signal difficult. Hence ECG signals needs to be preprocessed efficiently before its medical analysis. This paper describes an approach for preprocessing the noisy ECG signal with the use of Artificial Neural Network (ANN). For this work Self Organizing Map (SOM) of ANN is used. SOM is an unsupervised classifier which automatically distinguishes input data in groups based on the similarities in terms of features. Here various time domain features of ECG were provided as an input to SOM to form a classifier that classifies defective beats from normal beats. For this study, short duration ECG data from the physionet Mitdb database were used. The beats were segmented based on foot detection and the fiducial points were extracted. Some beats of ECG data were mixed with noise collected from the accelerometer. Based on the fiducial points, beat wise features were extracted which were fed to the input of SOM. The SOM will then classify the beats according to their morphology. Similar looking beats will stay in one group. So, by this method it can be easier to classify corrupted beats from the ECG signal. The correct classification of normal and abnormal beats was visually estimated from the weight distance plot of SOM.

articleTitle: A quantum study on digital image noises and their in-depth clusterization
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper, we represented a detailed survey of various types of Noise and its applications. Image processing is a field of study and research where we process raw images with the help of various functions or the input can be any parameter of the picture that we need to process. Noise as we all know as Unwanted Signal is responsible for Degradation of pictures in terms of Quality and Detailing. The primary source of Noise can be when we capture a picture, due to slow Shutter Speed, Temperature. Some noises are beneficial for us like noise is used in Posterization, Sharpness and in Dither. So, implementing an efficient noise removal technique is the utmost need today to harness each and every required detail. Nowadays we have effective Algorithms and Codes that can harness noise to enhance the image quality at any integral level of our choice. Every Image Processing Technique has its own advantages and disadvantages. We have to identify which kind of Algorithm will help us in getting the desired result. In this paper, we represented the survey of various kinds of Noise in Digital Image and we presented their effects in a particular Image.

articleTitle: Broadbanding of substrate integrated waveguide based slotted array antenna using dual slot configuration
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: This study represents some initial observations of the design of a Substrate Integrated Waveguide based Slotted Array Antenna using the concept of dual longitudinal slots to induce multiple closely spaced resonances. The simulated two element linear array exhibits enhanced Impedance Bandwidth characteristics of greater than 10% at a return loss of -15 decibels when compared to conventional single slotted design technique. A stable linearly polarized radiation pattern bandwidth of over 12% is also obtained with low side lobe levels & a very good cross polar isolation of around 30 decibels at the target frequency of 9.6GHz.

articleTitle: Lossy image compression using SVD coding, compressive autoencoders, and prediction error-vector quantization
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Now-a-days due to the huge increase in the size of image data Lossy Image Compression is highly used to reduce the image size but without having huge data loss. Image compression using SVD coding algorithm, Compressive Encoders and using prediction Error and Vectorization ratio are proved to have numerous application in image compression. Image compression using SVD coding algorithm involves refactoring of a digital image into three matrixes. Refactoring is achieved by using singular values, and the image is represented with a smaller set of values. Though, encoders cannot directly optimize due to the inherentNon-differentiability of the compression loss but it is out performing recently proposed approaches based on RNNs. The PE-VQ method is based on Prediction Error and Vector Quantisation techniques where image performance is determined using compression ratio and PSNR values using databases namely CLEF med 2009, Corel 1k and standard images like Lena, Barbara etc. Thus, in this research article a comparative study of these three techniquesis carried out where their image quality and compression ratio is examined by using the PSNR values and compression ratios.

articleTitle: Novel optical modulator using junction-less metal gate MOS phase shifter on SOI platform
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper, we report preliminary results for a novel optical intensity modulator employing metal oxide semi-conductor (MOS) phase shifter having metal gate instead of poly-silicon gate. The phase shifter is junction-less and uses different work function metal for electrodes. A Mach-Zehnder Modulator (MZM) based on this MOS phase shifter is realized on silicon on insulator (SOI) platform having 220 nm device layer thickness. As the proposed modulator does not use any embedded PN or PIN phase-shifter, it offers high speed operation along with negligible power consumption. Numerical simulations are performed to estimate the performance of the modulator using commercially available TCAD and mode solver tools. Results indicate that the modulator offers ~ 11.5 dB of extinction ratio (ER) and very low insertion loss (IL) of ~ 0.2 dB when the MOS phase shifter has a length of 300 μm and v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</sub> equal to 4.3 V. The transient analysis confirms the device operating speed up to ~ 21 GHz, with a 3-dB bandwidth of -7.3 GHz.

articleTitle: Study of FWM effects in WDM system: A review
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: CMOS integrated circuits; single electron transistors; nanoelectronics; logic design; microstrip antennas; cognitive radio; three-term control; transfer functions; numerical analysis; and logic circuits.

articleTitle: A sensor-based approach to monitor a specific plant sustainable environment with additional automated rehydration module
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In our daily life, owing to a strenuous schedule, it is not always feasible to nurture a plant in the proper manner. The task of understanding the specific requirements of individual plants and maintaining them is entirely laborintensive as well as time consuming. In this project, a method to technologically handle the process of fostering the desideratum of all plants have been proposed which focuses on making the job of monitoring a plants requirements easier. The proposed technology comprises of four modules namely, Moisture Detection and Rehydration Module, Temperature and Humidity Detection Module and Light Detection Module. Each module checks the specific parameters and consequently initiates the appropriate action. Firstly, the moisture detection module examines the moisture level of the soil at all times and on the basis of the data obtained it rehydrates the plant when required. Secondly, we have the temperature and humidity detection module which keeps track of the mentioned physical parameters and a Piezo buzzer connected to it indicates the prerequisite action to be taken if the parameters fluctuate. Then, we have the Light Detection Module which monitors the optimal light which is required for the sustainable growth and development of the plants. Arduino Uno is connected to Cayenne for fulfilling the above mentioned operations without the presence of any manual-labor. The proposed technology can be utilized as a home gardening solution, can be used for very sensitive plants which requires utmost care and lastly, provides a solution to meet the required moisture levels automatically.

articleTitle: Hybrid CMOS SET based gray to binary code converter
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Presently communication devices adhere to low power consuming high speed and low dimensional topology. In regard CMOS downscaling is a pivotal issue in device engineering. To the contrary, since the dawn of the previous decade ITRS roadmap demonstrated the limitations of CMOS downscaling. Consequently, new devices appeared among which single electronics is at driving seat. But empirical study reveals that SET alone cannot achieve triumph over CMOS with the available fabrication expertise. Thus hybridization of SET with CMOS is being largely pondered over and a new device principle augmented the concurrent Nano device engineering. Hybrid CMOS-SET (HCS), even in its embryonic stage catered enough interest both in industry and academia. The authors here intend to mobilize HCS in computational vicinity. Accordingly HCS is first improvised and the same is incorporated further to design a code converter. The developed HCS converter is simulated using SIMULINK of MATLAB and the results are quite satisfactory.

articleTitle: Optimization of the window layer in CdTe solar cell
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper, a CdTe thin film solar cell has been proposed by numerical analysis. The numerical simulation was done by PC1D simulator. We investigated the effect of minority carrier life time, thickness and doping concentration for achieving higher open circuit voltage(Voc), better Fill factor(FF) and efficiency(η). The highest conversion efficiency obtained was 17.06% (Voc = 0.611 V, Isc = 0.396 A, FF = 70.5%) with 1 μm CdTe absorber layer and 85 nm CdS window layer. The main aim of the work is to investigate on the CdS layer parameters (thickness, minority carrier life time) to achieve higher performance of the cell. In addition, the effect of carrier life time and doping concentration variation of the CdTe layer were investigated.

articleTitle: An efficient OCR based technique for barcode reading and editing
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The onset of wireless communication technology along with other hi-fi communication techniques has facilitated e-commerce with many aspects, such as time complexity and its easy reach to mankind. The modern shopping style has helped e-commerce in gaining its popularity with its comfort and convenience. The key idea here is to assist a person while shopping, by paying the exact bill for the very product he wants. Barcode reader and editor is such an idea with which the barcodes of the product can be read and can be corrected as well in necessary condition. This work deals with three major steps in materializing barcode reading and editing process. First of all the image of the barcode is enhanced by image enhancement techniques. Secondly, the barcode is read and finally the barcode is saved in a database for editing purpose. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technique is used in the decoding process. At the output the barcode image is displayed.

articleTitle: Study on temperature sensitivity of Si3N4 cladded silicon 2×2 MMI coupler
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper, we have numerically estimated the temperature sensitivity of silicon 2×2 multi-mode interference (MMI) coupler having silicon nitride as an upper cladding layer. The effect of refractive index and stress introduced by the cladding layer has been investigated using two MMI couplers having two different power splitting ratio. Moreover, the effect of sidewall slope angle of the waveguide in terms of its stress, birefringence and temperature sensitivity is also investigated numerically. The temperature sensitivity in terms of power splitting ratio for cladding thickness varying from 300 nm to 800 nm has been investigated in this paper. The results show that the stress induced by the cladding layer changes the temperature sensitivity of the MMI coupler in a very different way compared to the case when stress is not considered. Moreover, from the results it is found that the MMI couplers behave in similar fashion when the cladding layer thickness is beyond 500 nm.

articleTitle: Performance optimization of a soft and hard detector in cognitive radio environment using WARP
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Cognitive Radio, Software Defined radio Spectrum Sensing represents three development areas which are changing the world of Wireless Communication. The objective of this paper is to implement a new Hard and Soft detector based spectrum sensing method in a real time transmission network and optimize it. In particular, the aim is to detect the signals in the air, and estimate the power spectral density of the sources emitting these signals through collaborations of the receiver nodes. To achieve this, a receiver network based cooperative wideband spectrum sensing scheme is implemented using real time Transmission and receiving system using MATLAB and WARP environment. Two different types of Hard and Soft detection techniques have been compared with a new Softened Hard Detection scheme to show that the new method increases efficiency.

articleTitle: Carry look ahead adder design using CMOS output wired logic based majority gate
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Carry look ahead adder has been designed in the paper using the concept of majority gate and output wired logic. The circuit is designed for two bits and the power delay product is calculated for the carry look ahead adder. The transistor count for the proposed design of carry look ahead adder is less than the conventional design. The major advantage of the design is its fast computation and less power consumption and delay. The design has been verified using tanner tool.

articleTitle: Effect of temperature on modulational instability in normal region of CS2 core photonic crystal fiber with delayed nonlinear response
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: We theoretically investigated the effect of temperature on the process of modulation instability (MI) in the normal dispersive region of a CS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> core photonic crystal fiber (CSPCF) with delayed nonlinear response (DNR). The study shows that MI sidebands exhibit frequency shift in the normal dispersion region and the onset of such shift of Stokes and the anti-Stokes sidebands is highly dependent on temperature. Also, the temperature influences the bandwidth of Stokes and anti-Stokes sidebands and the same is reflected in the shift of optimum modulation frequency. However, the DNR plays a devastating role on the evolution of MI sidebands and suppress the later completely. With such a dominant behavior of the DNR, temperature does not play a major role except involving in the determination of the critical wavelength for the onset of MI suppression.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of frequency selective surface integrated microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper a wide stop band frequency selective surface(FSS) integrated microstrip patch antenna is presented. Wideband patch type FSS consists of four rectangular patches of different dimensions to give more than 7 dB improvement in gain of the antenna. The FSS layer is placed beneath the microstrip patch antenna. The FSS is responsible for increase in gain of the antenna. Characteristics of the proposed structure are simulated using HFSS. The FSS layer provides a wide stop band response with more than 10 dB loss in the frequency range 6-8 (Ghz).

articleTitle: Development and validation of the source code for defining the optimal path of a mobile robot using genetic algorithm based TSP
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Room temperature cyclotron and, Superconducting cyclotron of VEC Centre Kolkata are the experimental facilities being offered for the acceleration of multiply charged heavy positive ions as well as light ions at different energy levels. There exists high intensity of mixed radiation and neutron flux in the cyclotron vault, pit area during the operation of cyclotron. In order to acquire various field information including near real-time video from those inaccessible areas with fixed obstacles navigation of a mobile robot through several intermediate nodes following a fixed path can be a probable solution. In the path planning strategy of a mobile robot to reach the target location may or may not be an optimal one. This paper has concentrated on the development and verification of the source code written in C to find out the optimal path for a mobile robot traversing through several nodes using the concept of Travelling Salesman Problem applying Genetic Algorithm. Superconducting Cyclotron Vault with fixed obstacles has been considered as the target space for defining the optimal path of the mobile robot. The validation of the code has been done by changing the number of initial population and increasing the number of generations. The concept of elitism has been incorporated to find out the optimal path (the most probable solution) among all the generations.

articleTitle: Hybrid CMOS SET based expandable hardware
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: For the last five decades, electronic devices matured enough as the transistor size shrunk considerably. There by a new paradigm of ultra small scale device technology appeared and fuelled post CMOS device research. Consequently a classical manifestation of the quantization of electron charge evolved which is referred as Coulomb blocked in single Electronics Technology. This new technology ushered numerous figure of merit in nm scale electronics and soon single electronics was encoded to design logic circuits. But empirical studies revealed the limitations of room temperature based single electronics fabrication. Later on by amalgamating single electronics with conventional CMOS, addressed the limiting factors of single electronics fabrication. The new device principle is attributed as “Hybrid CMOS Single Electronics”. Since the last decade this hybrid topology is considered to design logic circuits similar to CMOS. Here the authors integrate classical CMOS with the uprising single electronics to model an expandable hardware and study its effectiveness to meet the current needs.

articleTitle: Designing of an efficient microstrip satellite antenna for handoff between Pico satellites
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Various programs for developing the Pico satellite constellations in Low Earth Orbits are being proposed and designed these days. The key feature in these systems is the inter satellite links that enhance the applications of satellite constellations. In this paper, the procedure to build an efficient microstrip patch antenna suitable for such links is presented.

articleTitle: HCS based PLA adder gate using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Since the last decade Single electronics fascinated researchers worldwide owing to its Nano feature size, ultra-low power dissipation and high speed like novel device functionalities. But the fragility is that it suffers from few intrinsic limitations. Besides, it has been revealed that CMOS and Single Electronics are rather complementary and hybridizing them diminishes the shortcomings of each other. To the contrary hybrid CMOS-Single Electron Transistors combine both the merits of Single Electron Transistors and CMOS devices and thus it ensures to be a more convenient realization for nanometer-scale circuit design. But CMOS and Single Electron Transistors are unique in nature and require two different simulating environments; thus they have to be simulated separately. Hence two distinctive simulators are used to simulate hybrid CMOS Single Electron Transistor and it is typically more time consuming. In this regard the authors here demonstrate a probable approach to simulate both CMOS and SET in one simulator. For exemplifying the authors report a hybrid CMOS-Single Electron Transistor PLA ADDER gate using MATLAB simulator. The results mimic the ADDER logic adequately.

articleTitle: Room temperature operable single electronic encoded logic ALU designing
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Future computing system using high speed low power consuming nano electronic devices is a significant outcome of the empirical study of post CMOS devices. SingleElectronics, even in its embryonic stage revealed enormous potential in diminishing the shortcomings of conventional CMOS. Thorough study on SE ushered Single Electronic Encoded Logic and this led to new single electron devices. The authors here without confining themselves in the study of single electronic fabrication put a leap forward to design room temperature operable CMOS compatible equivalent single electron arithmetic logic unit. The proposed design includes simple 1-bit ALU, the operation of which can be further extended to MIPS ALU designing. The authors admit that it is fascinating but painstaking endeavor.

articleTitle: Identification of amino acid properties using electrical codon network
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Extensive research activities in modeling electrical network of biological system have captured the interest of several researchers in recent years. Codons are the basic elements in DNA sequence which specify unique amino acids and form protein. Total 64 codons are modeled using passive ladder circuit consisting L and C to identify the properties of 20 amino acids. Corresponding circuits are converted into transfer function models to find out the correlations between simulated electrical responses and biological properties. The model responses are examined based on the amino acid properties such as hydrophobic or hydrophilic, aliphatic or aromatic etc. to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Equality detector — An attempt for commercial spintronics design
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Spintronics has ushered in a new horizon in post CMOS nano-electronics. The merits of Spintronics convinced spintronic researchers to mould spin topology in single spin logic. Consequently, new Spintronic devices emerged. Now Spintronic research aims to mobilize single spin logic for commercial production. In this regard, here, the authors attempt to design an Equality Detector using single spin logic. Initially, the authors incorporated MATLAB based spintronics simulator platform which has been earlier designed by Gope.et.al., and has been reported in reputed scientific reports. Straight off, the simulated circuitry mimics conventional CMOS logic and therefore the authors here advocate the incorporation of spintronics in future commercial appliances. Needless to say, that the test-bench results are in good agreement with spin physics and comply with the paradigm of post CMOS nano-electronics.

articleTitle: Zero dispersion photonic crystal fibers with low loss
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Four different Photonic Crystal Fibers (PCFs) with variation in ratio of diameter of air holes and hole to hole spacing (d/∧) has been investigated. Two different ratio of (d/∧) equals to 0.5 and 0.6 has been made in different quadrants of hexagonal PCF structures. Structure C with uniform distribution of (d/∧)= 0.6 shows excellent results. Besides all the structures reports very low dispersion and very low loss.

articleTitle: Study of energy optimization in optical networks: A review
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper we have discussed about the power consumption in an optical network. The study of various papers describes that the wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) is a technique which meets the increasing demand of bandwidth. Also there is more consumption of energy, when data is transmitted from source to destination through channels. In optical network, energy is consumed by the routers, links, network components etc. To minimize the energy consumption lots of techniques and algorithms has been defined.

articleTitle: Proposal of a transmon-based high bandwidth quantum router
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Larger bandwidth is an ever increasing demand of any communication system. Due to the unique device features, transmon is proposed to use in quantum communication. Not only as a quantum router, but transmon can also be used as quantum Josephson parametric amplifier. Josephson parametric amplifier provides high gain-bandwidth product which can be increased to a level beyond the traditional gain-bandwidth product. The larger bandwidth in Josephson parametric amplifier is achievable by appropriate impedance engineering which can be integrated to the hardware of the transmon-based router. We proposed here a quantum router with wider bandwidth and it is shown that the gain profile is very flat with a wide frequency of the quantum router.

articleTitle: Study of the performance of a rotary kiln of a cement manufacturing industry using PID controller
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: A theoretical study has been carried out to find the performance of a rotary kiln in a cement manufacturing industry, where PID controller has been used to control the quality of the clinker. This is done by finding the transfer function, steady state errors due to application of different types of input signals, such as unit step, unit ramp, and parabolic and frequency response of the whole system. The overall gain of the system is found out and numerical calculations and results are simulated using ‘MATLAB’ software.

articleTitle: Cognitive science: A review
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Deciphering the process that goes at the backyard of a human brain while introspecting an information and training a machine to react the same way a human does to a particular situation (or an information) defines the theme of our work “Cognitive Science”. In our work we analyse various fields of cognitive science and subsequently its pros and cons with the help of some research papers. Lauding the exemplary work and effort put by the scientists in this field which forms an innate pillar of modern day technology, yet we comprehend that there are lot of assumptions and conjectures rather than pertinent testimony and demonstration supporting it.

articleTitle: Single electron encoded logic decision-making system — A case study
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Single Electronics is a major role-player in today's Nano-device Engineering. It has matured from the very scrap of Single Electron Transistor and concurrently typical Single Electron Encoded Logic-based devices are designed in room-temperature operation. Thanks to excellent fabrication techniques that has molded single electronics into robust Nano-device. These devices are of extremely high speed and consume least power and also possess numerical figure of merit compared to conventional CMOS topologies. Being highly motivated by the virtues of single electronics in present context, the authors here endeavored a ‘Decision-making’ or ‘Prediction-type’ Single Electron Encoded Logic Circuit to meet the current needs. More specifically the designed Single Electron Decision-making Tool is empirically studied using SIMON simulator and the results are quite satisfactory.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of smile detection using Adaboost algorithms
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Face Pose is described as the combination of fixed and movable motions. The fixed and movable motions are associated in such a way that they cannot be separated from one another. Rigid motion is generally related with facial poses, whereas movable motion gets associated with facial expression. For separating one another, a normalized SVD decomposition technique had been utilized. Smile forms a part of facial expression and face pose. Smile detection has many applications in estimating gender, age, etc. This research article discusses two research articles published during 2012 and 2015. These two research articles were proposed novel technique on smile detection using Adaboost algorithms and achieved better performance. They used a database known as GENKI4K for experiment and analysis. Adaboost provided stepwise learning of a nonlinear classification function. It was focused to consider a collection of distinguishing coded features for face recognition. They chosen and combined weak classifiers depending on intensity differences to form a strong classifier. The 2012 research article achieved 89.55% and 2015 research article achieved 96.41% accuracy.

articleTitle: A case study of spin-computing device using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The complexity of computation increased manifold since the very inception of high speed low power consuming CMOS devices. In addition, the scaling down of CMOS devices significantly increased the computing speed. Consequently, new computing devices with highest speed has been commercialized. Spin based electronics or Spintronics is a novel candidate in the device vicinity and Spintronics made computing devices are concurrently attracting persons both of industry and academia. Since the last decade, the spin degree of freedom is acknowledged by Spintronic Researchers. They have sincerely attributed the spin physics in quantum dot and single spin logic is derived hereinafter. The single spin logic is incorporated in high speed ‘Spin-computing devices’ to shape the future consumable electronics. Here the authors endeavored a complex ‘Spin-computing device’ using single spin logic and the device is simulated using MATLAB. The results satisfactorily reveal greater acceptability of ‘Spin-computing device’ in Spintronics era.

articleTitle: An analytical approach to improve stability and to enhance active & reactive power profile of a grid network mainly under fault condition
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The initiation of fault in the Power System introduces a high degree of transient behaviour leading to the flow of a high value of current causing damage to the entire system. Several techniques has been developed for limiting the high fault current within a very short span of time but it's a continuous & ongoing research for the enthusiastic power system researchers to obtain optimum performance of the grid network by connecting certain dynamic components in the network. The modeling of the proposed grid network has been done using MATLAB/Simulink simulation software and its analysis has been evaluated under fault condition. This paper presents an analytical approach to improve stability and to enhance active & reactive power profile of grid network mainly under fault condition. The system incorporates connection of FACTS device to the network. The use of FACTS device improves the network parameters and ensures the reliability of power flow after a huge transient in the power system. A process flow model is also presented to explain the operational performance of the proposed network.

articleTitle: Modeling and performance analysis of multiple area power system
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Modeling and performance analysis of multiple area power system in S-domain is described in the present article. PID controller is used for load frequency control of the proposed multiple area power system. The use of PID controller ensures the reliability of power flow after a huge load disturbance in the power system network. Optimum values of Proportional, Integral and Differential controller gain has been determined using optimal control algorithm for reliable operation of the proposed multiple area power system. A digital control algorithm is also proposed in place of PID controller to improve the performance of the power system.

articleTitle: Photonic crystal fibers with flattened dispersion and ultra low confinement loss
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: This paper presents two PCF structure with `Y' shaped core. One structure has horizontal `Y' and other has vertical `Y' shaped core. Both the structure reports higher birefringence. Structure with vertical `Y' shaped core has shown flattened low dispersion at 1.33μm and 1.55μm. Structure with vertical `Y' shaped core reports ultra low loss. Besides two structures simulated ensures to be endlessly single mode fibers. However vertical `Y' shaped core promises to be a better candidate for application in optical communication, optical sensors, medical purposes, soliton, supercontinnum generation and other non linear applications.

articleTitle: Challenges and opportunities in super-resolution fluorescence microscopy
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Most of our understanding of biological processes and structures takes place through various optical microscopic systems. This paper gives a brief overview of the recent developments of super-resolution microscopy. Finally it depicts how Super-resolution Fluorescence Microscopy can widely be used as a tool for cell to provide detailed biological information, which remained unobserved previously.

articleTitle: A noble approach to light the path trail using swarm technology
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Swarm intelligence (Intro SI) is the collective behaviour of decentralized, self-organized systems, natural or artificial. It is many minds working together. It is the first step in allowing people to pool their knowledge and insights into a single elevated intelligence. The objective is to light on a path trail by the leading robot, so that the rest of the robots could follow the trail to work as a unified system, thereby reducing time and manpower.

articleTitle: Group based location tracking in multi-tier small cell network
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Cost-effective location registration of mobile terminals in multi-tier small cell based mobile network is a challenging research area. The cost is measured in terms of message. This paper presents an analytical model of group based location registration method referred as G-LTrack. The multitier network is composed of large cell base stations such as macrocell and microcell base stations and femtocells as small cell base stations. The femtocells are deployed inside the macrocell or microcell coverage area. The number of mobile devices moving together for long duration form a group and their handoff from one large cell base station to another large cell base station is also occurred in group, to reduce the number of message transmission over the network. In this paper after handoff the location registration to the new large cell base station is also performed in group. The location is updated at the visitor location register. If the new base station consists of femtocells inside its coverage, then according to the access of femtocells by the group users they are registered under the femtocells. In our G-LTrack we have introduced a new database which is associated with the base station controller. This database contains the femtocell IDs under which the users are registered. If all the users in the group are not using femtocell, then only the IDs of the mobile devices accessing the femtocells are stored in the database along with the serving femtocell ID and group ID. When a mobile device belonging to the group has to be traced the database is checked. If the group ID of that mobile device is found, it is checked whether the device is using large cell or femtocell. Based on this information the respective femtocell or the large cell coverage area is searched. The cost consumption in the proposed approach is calculated. Simulation results show that the proposed method G-LTrack reduces the location update cost by 13–20% approximately than the individual location update scheme. Simulation results also show that G-LTrack reduces the paging or searching cost by 52–86% approximately than the existing scheme.

articleTitle: The effect of annealing on band gap and optical properties of CdS/CdS-TiO2 nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper, we studied the effect of annealing of CdS nanoparticles that were prepared using chemical precipitation technique. The synthesized material were characterized using TEM and it was found the size of the CdS nanoparticles were ~5 nm. The prepared nanoparticles were annealed using hot air oven at 120°C and microwave oven at 900 W for different amount of time in order to check the effect of annealing. It was found that the annealing of the nanoparticles has increased the optical absorbance and reduced the band gap of the material. Interestingly, microwave annealing enhanced the optical absorbance compared to the annealing using oven and the band gap of the material was found to be less in case of 60s microwave assisted annealing compared to the 3 hr hot-air oven treatment. Moreover, the time requirement for microwave annealing was significantly less than that of hot air oven annealing for obtaining similar optical characteristics. The study was also performed for CdS-TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanocomposites and a similar trend in band gap reduction was observed. This study of annealing will be helpful in tuning the band gap of the CdS and CdS-TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanocomposites for different optoelectronic applications.

articleTitle: Effect of bit rate and laser input power level in TDM/WDM hybrid link applications
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Time Division Multiplexing and Wavelength Division Multiplexing both play a key role in maximizing the bandwidth efficiency in their respective domains. This work is guided towards the advantage of implementing the hybrid multiplexing technique which further boosts the existing range of bandwidth utilization than possible from either of the multiplexing methods alone. The work discusses about an analysis of a TDM-WDM hybrid link setup with variations in TDM signal bit rates using a standard simulation environment. The paper also brings out a phenomena encountered during the realization of proto hybrid link with input laser power level and its mitigation method. Thus, paper includes few of the analysis results obtained during the performance evaluation of hybrid link.

articleTitle: Quantum cryptography: Overview, security issues and future challenges
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In recent years Quantum Cryptography gets more attention as well as becomes most promising cryptographic field for faster, effective and more secure communications. Quantum Cryptography is an art of science which overlap quantum properties of light under quantum mechanics on cryptographic task instead of current state of algorithms based on mathematical computing technology. Major algorithms for public key encryption and some digital signature scheme such as RSA, El Gamal cryptosystem, hash function are vulnerable at quantum adversaries. Most of the factoring problem can be broken by Shore's algorithm and quantum computer threatens other hand discrete logarithm problem. Our paper describes why modern cryptography contributes quantum cryptography, security issues and future goals of modern cryptography.

articleTitle: Comparative study of different techniques to design ultra wideband antenna in cognitive radio
publicationTitle: 2017 4th International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The Ultra Wide Band (UWB)radio technology has attracted much interest in academics, industrial and standardization activities. Transmission systems with instantaneous spectral occupancy of higher fractional bandwidth is characterized by UWB. The antenna is probably the most overlooked part of a RF (Radio Frequency) design. The range, performance, and legality of a RF link are critically dependent upon the antenna. The radio spectrum is the source that is needed to be utilized using cognitive radio (CR) system. Detecting primary users (PU) over the spectrum is one of the problems that we face in the cognitive radio system. Here the UHF (Ultra High Frequency) TV Band is specifically addressed which is a target band of IEEE802.22 standardization. The UHF TV band is 336MHz wider according to CCIR (Consultative Committee on International Radio) standards. One major challenge in designing a UWB antenna for UHF band is limiting the physical size of the antenna. The paper illustrates the successful design, implementation and testing of a UWB antenna for cognitive radios in the UHF TV Band. The antenna is simple, cheap and very compact and can be used in fixed transceivers. Different papers on various configurations of wideband antenna have been studied and the different antenna parameters have been verified. The microstrip antenna has advantages of being low profile, light in weight and cheap. In this paper we have designed and simulated a GPS micro strip antenna that perform wide band CP radiation. The proposed antenna consists of orbicular micro strip patch, a substrate of feeding network and a circular patch above and orbicular patch antenna fed by two coaxial wires that is considered as the base structure. The feeding network was designed and combined with the antenna. The proposed CP antenna can be designed by adjusting the dimensions of the inner and the outer radius of the orbicular patch to determine the operating frequency of the antenna. Then the parameters of the branch line directional coupler can be fine tuned to achieve the required frequency with good impedance matching.
